profile.summary: UniSpec predicts the full set of fragment ion series for a peptide, not only b and y ions, and is sensitive to the collision energy. The input is a spectrum label: sequence, charge, modifications and collision energy. The output is a predicted intensity for each entry of a fixed fragment dictionary, written out as an msp spectral library. The released model, UniSpec23, ships in the repository with its dictionary and accessory files.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: UniSpec predicts into a fixed dictionary of fragment ions rather than a binned spectrum. The released model config has 9 blocks, an embedding size of 256, 38 input channels, a sequence length of 40 and an output dimension of 7919, which is the size of the fragment dictionary. Attention head sizes are 16, 16 and 64, and the last filter width is 512. The training config has an option CEembed for embedding the collision energy; in the released UniSpec23 config it is false. A dictionary usage criteria file and ion statistics from training ship beside the checkpoint and are used when a prediction is written.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One trained model is released, saved_models/unispec23, holding the checkpoint ckpt_epoch16_0.9263 of about 59.8 MB with its dictionary, model config, criteria, modifications list and training ion statistics. The prediction config is preset to those paths. Koina also hosts a version of UniSpec that returns the top 200 predicted peaks by intensity, which is not the same output as the local model, so a result should say which was used. The training and evaluation datasets are not in the repository: the configs point to a Zenodo download. This page read the repository at commit 60574023.

sections.title: How the benchmark used it
sections.body: PepSpecBench calls UniSpec an attention-based dictionary model of about 12M parameters and groups it with the full-spectrum and dictionary models whose wider ion space is projected into the benchmark's shared fragment layout. All six baselines were retrained on the benchmark data under backbone-disjoint splits, so that figure and those results describe the benchmark's retrained model, not the released UniSpec23 checkpoint.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Deep learning model predicting full fragment ion peptide spectra over a fixed ion dictionary.

quotes.text: Implementation of UniSpec, a deep learning model for predicting full fragment ion peptide spectra.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Attention network of 9 blocks, embedding size 256, head sizes 16, 16 and 64, last filter width 512, 38 input channels and 7919 outputs.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A spectrum label of sequence, charge, modifications and collision energy, either in the complete form {seq}/{charge}_{mods}_{ev}eV_NCE{nce} or as space separated fields, or an msp dataset.

run_guide.summary: Clone the repository at the pinned commit and predict an msp library with the released UniSpec23 model.
prerequisites: Python with PyTorch and PyYAML; the repository sources read give no requirements file or version floors.
A GPU is expected by default: predict.yaml sets enable_gpu to True.
A label file or an msp dataset to predict; the evaluation datasets come from the UniSpec Zenodo download named in the configs.

git clone https://github.com/usnistgov/UniSpec
cd UniSpec
git checkout --detach 605740231e049b6100bc8b36104ccb0b1b452e86
